headline: Kampung Baru Master Redevelopment Remains Unrealised; PKB Has Delivered Smaller Projects
context: The Kampung Baru master redevelopment remains unrealised after four decades. PKB lists completed Kampong Bharu-area projects, but the master plan has not been delivered. The separate Kampung Sungai Baru sub-project (328 properties) moved forward in 2025.

cards.big: Forty years of proposals, no master redevelopment delivered. PKB lists completed smaller projects; the comprehensive plan has not begun.
cards.sub: PKB's operational area covers about 121.7 hectares (300.73 acres). About 18,000 people lived in Kampung Baru's seven villages in 2010, a 2016 study found.

cards.big: Kampung Baru sits beside the KLCC core. Its land holds Malay Agricultural Settlement status, gazetted in 1900.
cards.sub: In October 2025 the minister called overlapping ownership 'one of the biggest hurdles' for such land. A 2016 study adds small lots and inheritance claims.

cards.big: About 18,000 people lived in Kampung Baru in 2010, a 2016 study found. Many trace household ties to the 1899 founding of the settlement.
cards.sub: Heritage value is officially recognised: Act 733 defines the 'interest of the Malays' to include their heritage, customs and culture in Kampong Bharu.

cards.big: PKB (Perbadanan Pembangunan Kampong Bharu), set up in 2012, has delivered specific projects but not the comprehensive master redevelopment.
cards.sub: Act 733 makes PKB the principal coordinating body for development. Its project page lists two completed projects as of November 2026.

cards.big: Kampung Baru is not a real estate problem. It is the unresolved question of whether Malay heritage and KLCC-grade land economics can coexist on the same blocks.
Like a historic neighbourhood where the heirs and the city disagree on renovation: four decades of blueprints, only patchwork delivery.
cards.sub: Kg Sungai Baru moved through acquisition, compensation, court processes and government intervention, not consensus among the owners of its 328 properties.

cards.big: The path forward is not a bigger plan. It is structured smaller-block consolidation with heritage and Malay-ownership protections built into each phase.
